newsitem.title: UK: M&S, retailers gain amid consumer strength.
newsitem.headline: M&S, retailers gain amid consumer strength.

text.p: Shares in Marks & Spencer Plc and other leading UK retailers rose on Thursday as a report suggested consumer demand remained robust and renewed sterling strength dented recent enthusiasm for overseas earners, dealers said.

Rallying from recent losses, M&S shares were up 16-1/2p to a near record 593 by 1417 GMT while Next Plc was up 27p to 764-1/2. Kingfisher Plc was up 17p to 719-1/2 and Great Universal Stores Plc was up 4-1/2p to 628.

Business Strategies Ltd said consumer confidence in Britain jumped sharply after the May 1 election, with optimism about the economy reaching its highest level since the survey began in the early 1980s.
However the survey also found consumers planning to raise their savings and said there was no sign of a runaway boom. It said there was scant justification for further UK interest rate rises.
Dealers said the report, along with a rebound in sterling, had revived interest in retailers. "People are back looking at the domestics again," said one.
